title: Zayd ibn Harithah
hookLine: the only companion named in the Qur'an (33:37)

cards: Read the Qur'an cover to cover and you meet prophets by name: Abraham, Moses, Jesus, Joseph. You meet Pharaoh. You meet Mary.
The men and women around the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, are another matter. The book speaks about them, to them, and of what they did, often without saying who.
Then, in the thirty-third surah, one plain name appears. Not a king. Not a prophet.
A man who came into the Prophet's house as a slave. Tradition says he is the only companion the Qur'an names. Today: Zayd.

teach.b: The biographies tell that Zayd was taken as a boy and sold, and ended up in Khadijah's household, and she gave him to Muhammad before the revelation began. Muhammad freed him.
They also tell that Zayd's father and uncle tracked him down and came to buy him back, and Zayd, given the choice to go home, chose to stay.
That story comes from the sira, not from the Qur'an or Bukhari, so hold it as the tradition's telling. What Bukhari does record is what people called him.
Abdullah ibn Umar said: we used to call him Zayd ibn Muhammad, Zayd son of Muhammad, until the verse came telling believers to call adopted children by their real fathers.
That is the same surah, verse five. A little later, verse forty says, in Pickthall's words: "Muhammad is not the father of any man among you."
So Zayd lost a name, and went back to being Zayd ibn Harithah, son of his own father. And in that same surah, he gained another.
Verse thirty-seven speaks to the Prophet about Zayd's marriage to Zaynab and its ending, and in the middle of it the text says his name: Zayd.
It is a hard passage, about a marriage that did not hold and a custom being changed, and commentators read it carefully. People had called him the son of the Prophet.
The book took that title away, and then wrote his own name into revelation. The book that names prophets also names him. Whenever someone recites that verse, his name is said aloud.

how: Muslims learn Zayd ibn Harithah's story from the sira and from Surah al-Ahzab, where verse 37 names him; reciters say his name whenever they reach that verse.

games.q: you are Zayd, freed in the Prophet's house. your father and uncle have found you and offer to take you home. what do you do?
games.why: the biographies tell that he chose to stay. it's a story from the sira, not the Qur'an or Bukhari.

practice: Go back over his story slowly: a boy taken from home, a household that freed him, a name people gave him, a verse that gave back his father's name, and a verse that says his own.
If a Qur'an is nearby, you might find surah thirty-three, verse thirty-seven, and look for his name on the page. If you pray, you can ask for those who were taken from home.
